Announcing The Griddies for 2026!

Each year volunteers from The Academy here gather your votes to honor the best puzzle of the year in each category: M-W, TH, FRI-SAT, and SUN. Nominations for POYs will commence on December 1 and run until the 31st. After balloting in the first weeks of January, winners will be announced in the third week of January. Voting is easy, anonymous, and fun! Even more fun is going back through the archives of 2026 and noting your favorites. 

I can use some help! My two fellow volunteers from last year are too committed to other projects this year, so right now it’s just me. If you’d like to help out with the Griddies, you’d be 1) drumming up participation in Comments, 2) writing up nominated puzzles (giving a short description for balloting purposes, and 3) help out with gathering nominations and votes and constructing the ballot. If interested, please REPLY under this message and we’ll figure it out.
Some tough clues here, but 29D in particular is barbaric.

Just today I had soup dumplings, among other similar items, for lunch, without knowing that their Chinese name was XIAO LONG BAO!

Amazingly, this one showed a good deal of resistance, and yet I finished about 7% faster than my Saturday average.  A lot of that was due to the fact that I can, at this stage in my solving experience, make educated guesses about some answers and wind up being right in the end.  MOVIE GENRE for [Action, e.g.] is just one of many.  On the other hand, KNITWORTHY came entirely on crosses, and I never even saw it until I was done.
Speedy one at 50% of my average Saturday time. Meanwhile I should be going to sleep, but now my stomach is growling with thoughts of XIAOLONGBAO, NOODLE, and SOBA...
Charming puzzle. Loved Zhou Zhang's note on xwordinfo.com.

Hi! Zhou's delightful,
as are her crossword puzzles
What a friend I have! 🤓

I had to use check puzzle to find the square I had wrong. I don’t think a gun to my head would’ve helped me figure it out ever. X marked the spot. Fun puzzle.

I’m still working on the top half of Friday’s puzzle.
Ok, Boomer[angs]!

"I know all the birds in the genus Corvus!"
"That's nothing to crow about."

("I'm raven about it anyway.")

Another stone winner from Zhou Zhang.  There were so many bright entries like KNITWORTHY (which I only got by remembering the spongeworthy episode of Seinfeld) and FATFINGERED (a concept I a intimately familiar with, as fatfingering seriously slows my solving experience). FAQIR and XIAOLONGBAO in the same quadrant, bravo!

I had several SNAFUS, including misspelling STYNE and entering Reading instead of NEAREST, (I only had the EA and felt very smug about Reading).  

I’m a devotee of COVERSONGS, especially those which reinterpret and surpass the original, like Judy Collins’s two versions of Just Like Tom Thumb’s Blues, and liked the clue [They’re played by different people].

Finally, a shoutout to my law school alma mater. Go Quakers.

I enjoyed every minute of this one, even when I thought it might defeat me.
"Let us cross words from various unrelated foreign languages and use the 'word' CYCLERS, for that will be fun," said no one ever.

Always look forward to Zhou’s puzzles and can’t wait to congratulate her once she hits for the CYCLE(R).

This was an unassuming looking grid at first glance but it packs a lot of wallop and almost KO’d me especially the NW. I had nothing there until the Crocodile Hunter saved me (crikey!) That and BADNEWS (clue of the day in my opinion) got me WEBBY and NOODLE, ___MAN got me IRONMAN, and then ISUREHOPESO. But even that didn’t get me far until I finally pulled out QUAD (embarrassing lapse for a pediatrician!) and most of the rest of it. I confess I ran the alphabet for the X, my best guess was FINE (set as in done?) but I admit that was another star clue today. Felt like it could be so many things, I was entertaining DEUX and even RIVE (set of banks for the Seine?). But FIXE was perfect.

Many sparkling entries and clues today from Zhou, I also loved KNITWORTHY and FATFINGERED. Surprised that Strapless got a question mark on a Saturday because it literally means UNHARNESSED. (I have another fun clue for that: “Like one who just can’t take a yoke?”)

Anyway, a great puzzle to NOODLE on (SOBA or udon)—thanks Zhou!
Anyone with more knowledge than me volunteer to put XIAO LONG BAO in the BAO (or part of Baozi) Wikipedia entries?  In case anyone uses it again?

I honestly think Zhou has it in for me.

I seem to remember this name when I fail to solve without help.

In this case it was the upper left (NW)...FIXE crossing XIAOLONGBAO and FAQIR was just more than I could muster.

Well, rats.  I guess I need to bone up on my French, my Chinese cooking, my Nereids, my shades of pink, and my "Funny Girl" composers.  Not to mention my types of cotton.

Way too difficult for me.

This was an absolute banger. Loved every square. I credit Denver's own James Beard-winning Penelope Wong's Yuan Wonton and an explosion of other outstanding dumpling places around this city over the past four years for letting me get XIAO LONG BAO without crosses!

What a pleasant solve, nothing to critique here.
I finished this puzzle just before lunchtime, and it provided me with a suggestion of what to have.

Very tough today. I didn't know the full name of the dumpling, couldn't come up with the holy person (and would have spelled it with a K if I'd thought of it at all), and had to go to Wikipedia for a list of the Nereids. Who knew there were so many? I liked FATFINGERED, was surprised by GRINGOS (it seems like it would be a retired word by now), never would have come up with RPG without the crosses. About the only things I was really confident of  first time through were IRWIN and PIMA.

Is there an award for Natick of the year?

If so, I vote 1D and 17A, FIXE and XIAOLONGBAO.  Took me way too long to get off of FINE (yeah yeah...French films which project "Fin" ("set" = "done" = "finished" = "end" ?) at the end have no "e" at the end of the word but I have no French and figured maybe it's some gendered variant or declension or inflection until I realized I was hungry and then "price FIXE" hit me and I still had zero clue of any part of 17A except BAO which I filled in at the beginning...STEAMINGBAO maybe?...but, hey, XIAO looks Chinese enough and suddenly solved music plays...)

Sturday Saturday, ma'am.

It seemed they switched the Friday and Saturday again... except for the upper left which just killed me.  I've never seen Fakir spelled that way, I didn't know that Chinese name for dumplings, didn't know the Nereid or Watts, didn't decode the race for too long, and was holding on to The Hurt.

There's a reason "cyclers" is a debut - it's not very good.  Ditto for "yawps", whatever that's supposed to be.  I didn't appreciate "EVO" either.  I had thought I liked this constructor's work but perhaps that was premature...

Fast enough in the end, but I found this hard and unlikeable.  (XWStats just says Average.)
12D [Boasts of] I gotta CROW "If I were a very, ordinary, everyday thing I'd never be heard, cockadoodaling round like a bird" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lMurEg-U6HA

I absolutely loved this puzzle. I finished in under half of my Saturday puzzle average time, so I understand those questioning the day assignment, but the fill was excellent. 

FAT FINGERED and XIAO LONG BAO made me so happy. Great puzzle.

I'm getting a sense of deja vu here.

I am postulating, prior to going to the trouble of gathering evidence, that Zhou's puzzles tend to be full of clues that some absolutely love and some absolutely hate.  

Consequently, I think there's a greater divergence in opinion about the puzzles than is typical.

Now I'll try to find the evidence.  But you can just assume I'm right unless and until you hear from me otherwise.

I'm not sure if the sweater depicted in the Wordplay column photo is really 27D [Like someone who would treasure a thoughtful handmade gift, in slang] KNITWORTHY. Here's a popular sweater pattern on Ravelry, a knitting website. If you click on the "Projects" link at the top of the page, you can see over 3000 iterations of this pattern by various knitters. https://www.ravelry.com/patterns/library/alpine-bloom The Ranunculus sweater pattern is also popular. Over 39,000 knitters have submitted photos of their finished Ranunculus sweaters. https://www.ravelry.com/patterns/library/ranunculus-3 The Sophie Scarf pattern is the Taylor Swift of knitting patterns--with over 61000 projects submitted!

Dear lord. Brutal from the start.

1D - crossing FIXE with two unknowns (for me), FAQIR and XIAO…

And no way for me to get through it with any sort of alphabet run because YAWPS was diabolical in the Middle East.

I went with YELPS because SOBe noodles seemed like a rational alternate spelling. And I still don’t really see how [“Listen…”] solves to NOW.

I mean, I get it… conversationally, one could be used for the other… but it’s not, like, *gettable* for me as a solver who started his journey PGE (Post Great Easening). That clue crossing with a random sound like YAWPS felt like something from the distant archives, when Saturday puzzles are still mostly much too hard for me.

Tonight was my first lookup in quite some time, and I’m glad I tapped out when I did, or I’d have been up all night.

Awesome puzzle. Thanks for the tussle!
I'm really wondering if KNITWORTHY is a thing. I haven't received anything knitted in a long time. Should I feel bad? Maybe some knitters out there can comment.
Brilliant. Absolutely brilliant.
Can someone explain 50D to me? I cannot figure this one out
The NW corner was way too hard for me, and not in a fun way. https://imgur.com/a/A2pAoYc

Personally, I enjoyed the knottiness here, a throwback to Saturdays of decades past. I can well understand why many found this puzzle frustrating, though; I'm no wizard, but I had luck on my side, I think.

And kudos to the commenters! Not once (yet) have I seen a successful solver berate or sniff at someone blowing off steam about their frustrating grapple with a tough grid. That's as it should be.
TIL hammy, fixe, ione, rpg, faqir and xiaolongbao. I’m glad for xiaolongbao that it made its debut today, but I now respectfully suggest it be permanently retired.

I didn't get what RES was until I came to the comments and saw, of course, it's REServation, like at a restaurant.

I thought it might be a meal made from whatever has been RESting in the fridge, similar to the Quebec expression "touski" for a meal made from Tout ce qui .... reste dans le frigo
The use of non-English terms is supposed to be limited to words that an English speaker might reasonably be expected to know. XIAO LONG BAO is most definitely outside of that boundary.

How long bro did it take to come up with this pile of steaming yummery?
Seriously though it was easily good enough to sweat it out. My favo(u)rites were the returning frequent fliers, and the sweater appreciators, which is a rare case of boom slang that does not appear to be a put down. That’s two memorable ones in a row, going upwards. 
ps can crosswords go upwards? Now there’s a thought…
Tip of the hat to Walter White for YAWP - from the other WW

Really enjoyed solving this one. The satisfaction of solving a Saturday puzzle will never wane for me! Must admit, if someone used the word “cyclers” to me, they’d get puzzled look from me. Even autocorrect isn’t happy!

Pretty hard but enjoyable, despite never having heard of the 'short' or 'informal' terms, like RPG, EVO, KOA, HOTS.

The composer seems very obscure to me, perhaps not to those in the US. On the bright side, only 2 names, I think. I've been on the verge of giving up on the crossword after some days with so many proper names that were also very obscure to me. Give me real clues, please! with words from dictionaries.

As far as I'm concerned, this puzzle ran on the correct day (took 2% less time than average).  Had doubts I would complete the NW corner, but somehow I finally came up with ISUREHOPESO.  So satisfying to think you've been beat, but then make it to the finish line.
I was stuck on the crossing of 1 D and 17 A, but then I had an idée.
Not totally up on my Greek names. EONE is not the Nereid, and ERWIN sounded correct! (Posted from five feet from an Australian.)

Zhou is one of my favorite constructors, so I will not say anything bad about the puzzle. Except that it totally defeated me.

That NW corner was brutal. Didn’t know the holy person, had no idea about the Chinese buns, and I had “mise” for “set in France”. 

CYCLERS (rather than cyclists) seemed weird to me, I’ve never heard of YAWPS, and I spelled STYNE wrong. (That one’s on me.) I did like FAT FINGERED and COOTIES, though!

This just wasn’t on my wavelength. But I still love Zhou and look forward to her next puzzle.

The common element in Zhou’s puzzles?  Spark.  Scintillating energy that makes the box vibrate.

Oh, there was knotty cluing, a gorgeous Times-debut grid design (look at that diamond in the middle!), and, for me, a brain-loving area of tooth-and-nail fight (the NW).  

These contributed to the spark, but it mainly came from newness, fresh long lovely answers we’ve never seen in the Times puzzle before.

There are twelve answer debuts, ten of them longs.  Many are wonderful additions to the Times oeuvre, including FAT FINGERED, I SURE HOPE SO, MOVIE GENRE, and WEBBY AWARD.  

Pop pop pop all over the place.  

Wit?  Just look at [Something that might be made for dinner, informally] for RES.   My favorite clue/answer? [Representations of some tree branches] for LINEAGES.  Magnificent!

I came to the box neutral, got jazzed when I saw your name atop the empty grid, Zhou, and left the puzzle fired up, ready to charge into the day.  Primo puzzle, ZZ.  Brava and thank you!

Very nice puzzle!

Especially once my [word after snap and before soup] brain finally said “xiaolong, farewell”  to the ideer that no letter on earth was going to fixe that mess in the top left corner.

Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious! 
So. Much. Fun. Thank you, Zhou Zhang!
The G in XIAOLONGBAO was my undoing. Bet it was a gimme for our Chinese solvers!

Found this one much easier than yesterday's, though that NW corner with FAQIR, XIAOLONGBAO, FIXE and QUAD made me work.

KNITWORTHY was new to me, as was YAWPS. "Prepared for another round" was simple and yet clever for RELOADED.

Done in about 30 minutes without any assistance. Hope that future Friday and Saturday puzzles will stay at the level of this week's puzzles.
What a clever delight for a Saturday morning!

17A: Did anyone else nerd out a bit with excitement seeing the clue for steamed buns and then the entry's spanner?

Not being a foodie, I landed on XIAOLONGBAO in a roundabout way. Had crosses at QUAD and IRONMAN in that sticky NW corner, and was pretty confident about FIXE, which gave me FAQIR (which sounded enough like "fakir" to seem reasonable) and ENDNOTE to confirm, then penciled in IONE and ASIN. Looked at XIAO_ _N and heard "Shaolin," as in the monastery (and the cult film Shaolin Soccer!), so entered XIAOLiN. Figured the entry must end in BAO from crossword experience, and the two together got me close enough to the Chinese buns for that whole corner and upper middle to fall. Let out a whoop! (Bet there'll be a lot of YAWPS! today, so just for variety.) 

Any other quirky corner stories out there, NW or elsewhere?
I was off to a great start, thinking I'd solve this Saturday clean, but then got stuck with the NW and SE corners. So disappointed I didn't figure out 55A myself :(

I was so proud that I knew from high school French that "set" was MISE. While that is true, it turns out so is FIXE. This stumbling block forced me to look up the full name for steamed bao -- my first look-up in months. 
(In the same corner, the "hammy neighbor" for QUAD was also beyond my grasp - clever clue, but I'm just not a gym rat.)
Sadly, I did not recognize the correct spelling of Whitman's thunderous cry, but was more familiar with Jo-Jo's "YOPP" in Horton Hears a Who.  "I'm here!"

The NW corner was especially hard because of the multiple reasonable options for “Set in France” crossed with foreign words most English-speakers aren’t familiar with. I started with mise (as in mise-en-scene) then fine (ok that doesn’t really work) and finally fixe after a lot of letter cycling. In retrospect it makes sense but it took awhile to get there. A good challenge for a Saturday IMO.

No lie.

We had XIAO LONG BAO 
last night for dinner.

Which ( obviously ) means
I’m having XIAO LONG BAO
for breakfast.

Felt like cheating when 
filled in those letters.


Love a ZZ puzz.

Extremely difficult, this to the point of not being fun or fair.  Without help of any kind I solved the entire puzzle except for 31A LISTEN - NOW, which is completely off the rails, but I get it, and 29D HARSHE CRIES - YAWPS, for which I entered YELPS.  YAWPS? Are you kidding me? I've heard if YIPS and YAPs, but YAWPS?  Pleeease.  This puzzle broke my no-help-of-any-kind streak of 25 days and I am not amused.

More from Zhou coming? I sure hope so! Loved everything about this puzzle including the wonderful constructor's note. So many aha moments. So many pat on the back moments. Favorites were for boomerangs, fat fingered, cooties, bad news and cover songs. Liked when I realized that 'Action' was a genre and not something a director yells.

Alas poor Fezzick. RIP Andre the GIANT. His appearance here reminded me of this little snippet of a scene in The Princess Bride, a version of which often transpires in these comments. https://clip.cafe/share/you-keep-using-word

I can never completely solve Ms. Zhang's crosswords.  Today's entries I have never heard of:  FAQIR, YAWPS, XIAOLONGBAO, or WEBBYAWARD.  While I'm not paranoid, I just know she comes up with such words (and clues) to personally drive me crazy.  Yeah, I'm going to stick with that.  It's a vendetta.  With that, I can claim some measure of mental stability.  :)
YAWPS?

Naticked by FAkIR crossing kUrD. Have never seen the Q spelling or known a hamstring called hammy. Pretty obscure, even for Saturday.  Couldn’t figure it out after I checked puzzle and knew which letters were wrong! Had to ask for solution. Was pleased to get all the other impossible stuff.

So much for stalling on my household chores this morning. If it weren't for TIRE (specifically the crossings with TEA ROSE and STYNE) I would've cracked this one in Wednesday time.

XIAO LONG BAO was gettable with the crossers but felt Natick-y to me. Maybe if I had a good dim sum place nearby it'd be a gimme?

Some gems in here, like FIXE, DEAD AIR, and BOOMERANGS, but overall this one felt way fast for a Saturday.

Well, I was on track for an annoyingly fast solve…and then there was FAQIR/FIXE/XIAOLONGBAO 🤣

Looking back, I was ridiculously slow to see FIXE, which should have been my entrée into that trio. But alas, it took me a solid half-hour to seriously consider X as the leading letter for that variety of bao, and only then did FIXE come to me.

Alrighty then, moving onto the next thing. Lovely day for a hike here in Vermont 🌞

Welp, this is all the time I can spend beating my head against 17A...be it right or wrong, I'm done (or done for.)  

I have a fairly close relationship with color...and TEA ROSE is not on the list.  It's fair to make up a name for a color as long as it bears some resemblance to the basic hue...  

I'll come back in a while (after I check the Answer Key) to report ...  Maybe add a mini-rant about 19A...
I knew it wasn't right, but for 3D, "Hammy neighbor", I filled in MOON, because a moon is adjacent to my hammy in the Denny's breakfast dish.

YAWPS!

But not as tough as yesterday's puzzle.

I started with a FATFINGERED FAkIR, so had to NOODLE on that a while. Was Hammy the Dane or a pig in 1984 or in Charlotte's Web?  :D
Pretty cruel to put FATFINGERED and UNHARNESSED right on top of each other! Grrr.

Flat out awful.  Far too much made up nonsense.  KNITWORTHY get serious. If that's a pun it's not fun.   Not dexterous = INEPT, sorry but no.  Let's just sit here with google open and look up trivia?  I'm glad you hard core folks liked it, but this was a big fat waste of time for me.
Gave up on the NW corner which felt pretty Naticky to me since it required knowledge of Arabic/Hindi, Spanish, Mandarin (I assume) and Greek mythology.
A knitworthy, praiseworthy puzzle, in my opinion.  Yes, it was hard.
I was not really into this one. But that’s on me, I suppose.

It took me a while.  I had Erwin instead of Irwin till the bitter end, intersecting with Ione, and xiaolongbao.  One of the harder corners in recent memory.  An excellent puzzle over all, though difficult to get a good toehold in.
Meh
Loved this one. We just vibed. Thanks!

Wait, is "set" not FIvE in French? Hmm, un du twa cat set...Oh, I skipped sank. (Yes, I know it's cinq, but I never took any French.)

I did, however, take Chinese, so I gave myself a facepalm when I realized it was XIAOLONG, which means "little dragon." It's also Bruce Lee's Chinese name. So there's today's lesson. I always order jiaozi or guotie, but it's nice to know the other dumpling.
Bam! No flyspecking. It took a while, but it was delicious fun crossing and recrossing until it just felt right. Great puzzle.

ATTENTION SOLVERS: If you solved this puzzle with no look-ups or help of any kind, your are SOMETHING SPECIAL.  You are a MASTER SOLVER.  Bravo! I am not a master solver, because although I am familiar with yelps, yips, and yaps, I was not able come up with YAWP.  I was also not able to get NOW from LISTEN. Now solvers, don't let this get you down. Just learn from this puizzle and move on.  It's actually good to get cut down to size from time to time. Ego management.

poem made from words in today’s puzzle 

joy to the word
a/ 
the cotton in your ears
that rock in your mouth
and the mystery that something
in a word made a flower…
turned the night pink
with wheels of spinning color 
that word a word that overflows your soup
d/
that adjective that noun that wallops round and branches into words that words would treasure…
lover words 
concerned words
intense feelings words 
building making totaling words into a tree of a/ 
song

I allowed myself to cheat on IRWIN, but it still didn't solve the puzzle for me.  I had FAKIR (not FAQIR, which I'm sure I've never seen spelled that way.)  This gave me KURD for the "Hammy neighbor".  Why?  Who's a Hammy?  Where is Hammy found?  Beats me.  Never thought of hamstring.

Bringing me to "set in France" where I wrote in FINI.  As in finished.  But the citation had to be END NOTE, so I changed 1D to FINE.  Leaving me with NIROLONGBAO -- as good a name for a Chinese bun as any other, I'd maintain.  Or AVER, as crosswords would have you maintain.

Don't ask.  I really had to use my NOODLE today, but to no avail as it turns out.  A really tough Saturday.  Favorite clue/answer?  FAT FINGERED is great and worth the price of admission.
Wowza! That NW corner required a second walk of the doggo and a third cup of coffee. First time in years. What a great puzzle!
Loved the possible misdirection at 25D, where even getting the first half, movie-, doesn't separate it from the command on set to the -genre.
I assume that KNITWORTHY has its origins in the Seinfeldian "Sponge-worthy". https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gfDyOyrY-zM Anyone from the knitting community care to confirm or contest this etymology?
Wow! So satisfying. The haiku is the icing on the cake! Thank you, Zhou Zhang!

Fun puzzle. Glared at KURD in the NW corner for a while before giving up and going for a lookup on the Chinese rolls.   

Perhaps describing 1A as a variant spelling for “fakir” would have unlocked QUAD and then XIAO — but wouldn’t have generated all that  eye-roll energy to channel into reading up on Arabic romanizations.

Columnist Caitlin struggled to describe why "Certain bearer’s burden" translated to BADNEWS, saying 'I picked up on “news cycle,” or maybe “bad news cycle.” '  How about the bearer of bad news?  I guess when one works from home there's nobody in the next cubicle to provide the "aha!" moment.
I'm here to CROW_ABOUT my wife finding me KNITWORTHY.
I loved it! (Save for CYCLERS…)
Awesome puzzle, so many aha moments from figuring out a tough clue from the crossings, and I sure was happy to have some gimmes to gain entry into harder ones!

What a great puzzle!  I can't remember how many times I've set this aside after starting around 5 AM this morning.  Made good progress at first but then stuck! stuck! in the SE.  

Had KNITWOR_ _ _ so focused on that and the light bulb went off.  I'll credit the neighboring Quakers for realizing THY. 

Great Saturday debut and many thanks.  

I also first had kUrD - figured "Hammy" was slang for Hammurabi.
Really tough NW corner but I persevered.  I like puzzles that I get few on the first time through but slowly build.
“Now stick with us cause Phineas and Ferb are gonna DOITALL!” “Mom, Phineas and Ferb are making a title sequence!”
The intersection of FIXE and XIAOLONGBAO took me way longer than it should have.
Ummm. No.

I guessed LINE---- very early, and then spent a good portion of an hour wondering what type of artwork the clue was referring to - LINEwork? LINEarts? I didn't fill in the second half until I got the G on the cross. Oh well, got there eventually!

This is what I get for not learning to speak French (I had "amis" at one point) or Mandarin, and for not memorizing the fifty names of the Nereids.

My youngest son, who spent a year in Nanjing, knew BAO, of course, but not the specific kind. I knew "fakir," but have never seen it spelled with a "q", so that "k" left me with "knee" as the anatomical neighbor, and I couldn't extricate myself from that snare.

I had left the NW for last. I'd figured out the rest. I was, as they say sometimes on the baking show, chuffed. But it was not to be.

Congratulations to those of you who got a clean solve. This one was too much for me, though.

Got lucky in NW, I started with faqir and fixe. The clue for fat-fingered seemed a stretch, but then I saw this online definition: "involving pressing the wrong button by accident when you are using a computer keyboard". Pleased with 22:05 overall, very good challenge.
Argh, I was all set to rail against the "hammy" clue, but on doing the reveal I saw it works. Ah, well. I would've beefed anyway.

Tripped myself up comically on "Set in France." My aural memory was interfering with my visual memory. Counting to ten in French, there was something that sounded like "set" but its English equivalent was more than four letters. I was pretty sure 5 sounded like Sanka coffee and might have a q in it somewhere. 

But the more I tried to count in French the more I began to doubt myself, and FI_E was certainly looking like FIvE. This is it--my mind can no longer be trusted.

So I dithered around for awhile and even fly-specked my grid before finally deciding to mentally run the alphabet on the _. By the time I got to "v" I was feeling pretty desperate. But then I got to X and the world made sense again after all.
Movie wasn't a theme?
FIXE/FAQIR/XIAOLONGBAO was so Naticky it tarnished an otherwise perfectly cromulent Saturday. Shame.

Whew. Tough but fair, and a little over my average time for a Saturday.

Also, a reminder to PNW solvers that registration for the inaugural Rain City Crossword Tournament in Seattle opened yesterday.
I really liked this one.  A good combination of aha moment wordplay, new for me items, and misdirects!  Congratulations on your Saturday!  Looking forward to your Tuesday!!
NW was a bit naticky for me and I couldn't finish. First time in a while.
I loved this puzzle except for the clue for 5D. I wish it was changed to smthg like “refreshed the page” instead of alluding to weapons.

Great difficulty level for a Saturday...except that I had to tap out on the crossing letters of FAQIR, FIXE, QUAD, and XIAOLONGBAO. Three foreign words and a punny clue I couldn't get after initially solving it wrong were just too much for me to puzzle through in the end.

Wonderful puzzle, Zhou Zhang! Was a real treat to solve.

TIL XIAOLONGBAO has the same number of letters as XWORDJUNKIE.
Enjoyed the puzzle.  Had to look up foreign entries in the NW corner.

What a great, challenging puzzle to start my long holiday week off. I'm pleased I've still got my streak of "no look-up" completions intact after wrestling with that tricky NW corner. Must remember to pick up a copy of the paper Times tomorrow for all that extra puzzly goodness in the Puzzle Mania section (I still have last year's Super Mega Crossword on my desk to complete during the holidays)!

People. "Foreign" languages? English is a "foreign" language to most of the folks who live on earth and ever have. Learning new words is fun! I would have expected a wee less insularity from the crossword solvers on this forum, especially since they seem to lean to the west in general. Plus go to a dim sum restaurant and eat some fabulous words, including bao of all kinds!
